# Temple Scroll Column 35 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 35 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**35:1** No one who is unclean from any human uncleanness shall enter My temple until he purifies himself.

**35:2** No man who has a discharge, or who has had an emission of seed, shall enter My temple.

**35:3** Not until the day he washes in water and the sun has set — then he may enter on the following day.

**35:4** No blind man shall enter it all his days, lest he defile My temple — for I dwell in its midst.

**35:5** No lame man, nor any man with a permanent blemish, shall enter and defile My temple.

**35:6** You shall warn all the sons of Israel about every uncleanness, so that they do not defile My temple.

**35:7** Every man who purifies himself from his discharge shall count seven days for his purification.

**35:8** On the eighth day he shall wash his garments and bathe his whole body in living water; then he shall be clean.

**35:9** Once he is clean, he may eat of the holy things, for the holy things are his food.

**35:10** Any man who has not yet completed his days of purification shall not eat of the holy things.

**35:11** He shall not enter My sanctuary until his days of purification are fulfilled.

**35:12** So that the sons of Israel do not make themselves unclean in the midst of their uncleanness and defile My temple, in which I dwell.

**35:13** Any man who lies with his wife and has an emission of seed shall not enter any part of the temple city for three days.

**35:14** No unclean person shall be seen in any part of My temple.

**35:15** You shall set watchmen at the gates of My temple to prevent any unclean person from entering it.

**35:16** For My temple is holy, and the place where I set My name is holy; it shall not be defiled.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus preserves "living water" (EMET) over "flowing water" (LOGOS) and "running water" (PNEUMA) — mayim chayyim is a technical term best rendered literally. "Unclean/uncleanness" preferred over "impure/impurity" for consistency with Leviticus translation conventions. "Watchmen" preferred over "guards" for its biblical register.*
